# Audio Lore Chapter 12 — The Eris Fabrication

**Narrative script for TTS generation.**

---

The destruction of Baoth in 421 BGD did not bring freedom. It brought the worst century in Erisdar's recorded history — Age 9, the Lost Era. Forty years of warlords carving up the corpse of the dragon empire. Twenty-five years of famine that killed forty percent of the population. Cities that had housed a hundred thousand souls under Baoth shrank to villages of ten thousand. Cannibalism was reported in the eastern provinces. The Lady-Protector of Grimmel ran the only functioning food distribution system on the continent.

And in the midst of this chaos — while children starved and warlords feasted and refugees fled burning cities — a woman appeared.

She claimed to be the incarnation of the goddess of Discord, Chaos, and Confusion — the deity who commanded all other gods. She performed miracles. She chanted down enormous monsters that had been terrorizing villages. She survived assassination attempts by walking through the attackers unharmed. She was executed publicly, her body displayed for three days — and on the third day, she rose again.

Her name was Eris.

She was a homunculus. A Shadow construct, engineered to pass as human. The monsters she defeated were Shadow-implanted — released specifically so she could appear to destroy them. The assassinations were staged by Shadow agents. The resurrection was a performance: she was never dead. Every miracle was a fabrication, every witness a dupe, every believer a victim of the oldest con in galactic history.

But she would not cure the sick. She would not heal the wounded. A desperate mother brought her dying child to Eris, begging for a miracle — any miracle. Eris looked at the child, looked at the mother, and said the words that would echo through history: "You are not worth it."

She could not cure the sick because the miracles were illusions. Curing real illness would have exposed the fraud. So she spun her inability as divine judgment. You are not worthy of healing. You are not worth the goddess's attention. Give everything you own to her church, and perhaps — perhaps — you will be found worthy in the next life.

It was monstrous. It was brilliant. It worked.

Her teachings were carefully engineered to serve the Shadow agenda. Kill your enemies — no forgiveness, no reconciliation. Live ascetically — give up your possessions to the Church. Trust the government — whatever authority exists, obey it. Donate everything — your land, your gold, your children as initiates.

The chaos of the Lost Era made people desperate. The Baothian civil servants who had lost everything. The starving farmers who had watched their children die. The refugees who had fled burning cities. Eris gave them one answer to the question "why did the world collapse?" — you were sinful. Give everything to me, and you will be saved.

Around 320 BGD — thirty years after her first appearance — Eris announced her departure. She ascended a prepared platform before a crowd of thousands, delivered her final sermon, and descended into a cave that collapsed behind her. No body was ever found. The legend would grow unchecked by evidence.

The Shadows had lost Baoth — their Phase Three pan-continental super-state. The Eris cult was their backup plan. Phase Four. And it was better than the original. An empire can be conquered. A religion cannot be killed. Within three centuries, the Erisian faith would dominate the continent. By 27 AGD, the Erisian Empire had been founded. Within six centuries, the Church controlled the spiritual lives of tens of millions — directing their beliefs, their donations, their obedience — all toward a goddess who never existed.

The Eris Fabrication is the most successful lie in Ge'orian history. It has outlasted empires, survived crusades, and adapted to every political change for over nine hundred years. The people who kneel in the cathedrals and light candles to the goddess of Chaos have no idea they are praying to a Shadow construct who told a dying child she was not worth saving.

And somewhere beneath the earth, the Hybrians are still pleased with their work.
